text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, which saves time for everyone on the team. One key practice is following naming conventions, such as using clear and meaningful names for variables and functions. Another important idea is keeping functions small and focused on a single task. This makes them easier to test and reuse. Finally, clean code supports maintainability, meaning it is simpler to fix bugs and add new features later. By writing readable code from the start, developers can work faster and avoid many common problems in the future.
